back: The total way of life of a people: language, beliefs, customs, norms, values, food, dress, arts, tools and institutions, passed on from generation to generation.
The network of relationships by blood and marriage, with duties and forms of address, linking the extended family and clan.
The things people make and use, e.g. pots, tools, houses, instruments.
The ideas, beliefs, norms, values and language that guide life, e.g. folk tales, proverbs, totem praises.
The chief's granary: a field worked by the community whose harvest helped people in need.

front: Name six features of indigenous Zimbabwean culture.
back: Language, family and kinship, totems, religion and beliefs, food, dress, music/dance/crafts, social organisation and leadership, communal values (any six).

front: How are totems linked to kinship?
back: People of the same totem count as relatives, so they do not marry each other.

front: Give three reasons indigenous norms and values matter.
back: Identity and belonging; moral guidance; social security (also unity, knowledge, heritage for tourism and arts).
